title: Adaptive presubmit router and lightweight toolchain bundle
author: Ava Patel
release_notes:
- Introduces an adaptive presubmit router that routes PRs to lightweight fastpath lanes based on touched paths and heuristic risk scoring.
- Adds a minimal toolchain bundle for local dev and CI warmup images to reduce test flakiness and cold start time.
- No API or runtime behavior changes; internal CI infra only.
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic presubmit pipelines have grown slow and brittle. Small iterative PRs (docs, small SDK fixes) incur the same full integration battery as large runtime changes which increases feedback time and developer context switching. This change introduces a presubmit router that categorizes PRs into fast, standard, and full lanes using a deterministic set of rules and a lightweight risk score computed from touched paths, labels, and historical flakiness.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a deterministic presubmit router service (ci/presubmit-router/) which evaluates PR metadata and outputs a lane decision. 2) Adds a minimal toolchain bundle image and accompanying scripts (scripts/toolchain-bundle/) to provide hermetic, fast warm images used by fastpath CI and local dev containers. 3) Reworks our .github workflow entrypoints to support conditional lane selection and staged job expansion. 4) Introduces a small shim library (packages/ci-utils) that other repos can call to mirror routing decisions locally (devcontainer and CI parity).

Design notes and tradeoffs: - Router criteria are intentionally conservative: fast lane excludes runtime, serving, infra, and docs that touch build tooling itself. The initial rule set is configurable via a simple YAML config checked into ci/presubmit-router/config.yaml. - The toolchain bundle is purposefully minimal (clang, go, node, python pinned versions) to avoid large image sizes; it reduces cold build variance and speeds up hotspot tests. - We deliberately avoid replacing the existing QA gates; this is a progressive optimization that only skips heavy jobs for low-risk PRs.

Checklist implemented: - [x] Presubmit router service implementation and unit tests. - [x] Workflow templates updated to call router and expand job matrix conditionally. - [x] Toolchain bundle image build scripts and README. - [x] Shim library with local router client and a thin CLI. - [x] Integration smoke: fastpath jobs exercised on a canary org. - [x] Docs: docs/ci/README.md describing rules and how to override.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind a feature flag defaulting to off. 2) Run canary on low-risk repos (docs, examples, sdk- typescript) for one week. 3) Collect fastpath hit/miss metrics and adjust rule set. 4) Gradually enable for more repos once flakiness < 1% and false-skip rate < 0.5%.

Backwards compatibility: Workflows maintain an opt-out label (ci/full) and an environment variable to force full runs. Existing presubmit behavior remains available.

Related: ENG-2992 for fastpath metrics collection and ENG-3010 for toolchain pinning policy. SUP-1128 tracked a support incident where a flaky test was exacerbated by cold toolchain images.

Testing summary: Unit tests cover router logic, e2e smoke in a sandbox org verified job expansion, toolchain bundle built and validated in both Linux and macOS runners. CI initially flagged a flaky lint job which was fixed by improving the linter wrapper to respect workspace node_modules in devcontainer images.
